item.title: McRaney case declined, ending NAMB lawsuit
item.description: SCOTUS declined to hear a years-long case brought by former Baptist state convention executive director Will McRaney against NAMB.

item.title: Voices: Sharia law and championing religious liberty
item.description: Jack Goodyear calls Christians not to participate in fearmongering but to embody the gospel by standing with religious minorities.

item.title: Around the State: HPU names five Currie-Strickland scholars
item.description: Howard Payne University named five students as Currie-Strickland scholars during the 18th annual Currie-Strickland Distinguished Lectures in Christian Ethics in February.

item.title: Historically Black churches receive millions in grants
item.description: Sixteenth Street Baptist Church in Birmingham, Ala., and Atlanta’s Ebenezer Baptist Church are among 33 Black churches receiving millions of dollars for preservation of their sacred and historic buildings.

item.title: BGCT Executive Board restructures, addresses challenges
item.description: The BGCT Executive Board restructured in its February meeting and heard updates on church property insurance and the Cooperative Program.

item.title: BGCT Executive Board approves CP task force
item.description: The Baptist General Convention of Texas Executive Board approved the creation of three new task forces and approved committee and board nominees and two relationship agreements.

item.title: Voices: The significance of Black hymns for all Christians
item.description: Dr. Roy Cotton Sr. shares the significance of Black hymns and hymnodists to the musical and devotional life of Baptists and all Christians.

item.title: Connect360: Sing and Shout to the Lord!
item.description: Lesson One in the Connect360 unit “Psalms: The Believer’s Prayer Book” focuses on Psalm 66:1–20.

item.title: Religious ties shape how Black Americans define family
item.description: Black Christians are more likely than religiously unaffiliated to consider nonrelatives a part of their families, study shows.

item.title: On the Move: Stringer, Treviño
item.description: Pastoral and associational changes noted in Richmond, Santa Fe, Beeville, and Mathis.
